apartments.title: Apartments in Tashkent city center
apartments.lead: Two apartments, both a walk from Amir Timur Square. We host them ourselves, so the person who answers your message is the person who hands you the keys.
apartments.section-lead: We keep exactly two apartments and look after both of them personally. That is the whole inventory, which is why we can promise the photos match what you walk into, and why the calendar fills up early in spring and autumn.

hero.photo: Cream-plastered residential facade in central Tashkent photographed in late afternoon light, deep-red architectural accents around the balconies, a low camera angle, clean geometric composition, warm grading, faint film grain, no people, 4:3 landscape.

list.title: Both apartments in detail
list.lead: Read the two of them side by side and tell us which one suits your dates. Every square metre, every floor number and every photo brief below describes the flat you will actually walk into, because we hand over the keys ourselves.

location.title: Why the centre is worth it
location.lead: Tashkent is a big, flat, generously spaced city, and staying in the wrong district turns every evening into a taxi ride. Both of our apartments sit inside the ring where the things you came for are within walking distance of each other.

location.link-contact: Ask us what is on this week

square.title: Amir Timur Square
square.text: The square is the geographic and social centre of Tashkent, ringed by the Hotel Uzbekistan, the Amir Timur Museum and a stand of chinar trees old enough to have shaded several republics. From either apartment you reach it on foot in ten to fifteen minutes, and once you are there the rest of the historic centre unfolds without a single taxi.

broadway.title: Broadway and Sailgokh Street
broadway.text: Locals call the pedestrian stretch running off the square Broadway, and it is where Tashkent goes in the evening: portrait painters, chess tables, corn sellers, small stages and a permanent hum of families walking nowhere in particular. It is two minutes further than the square and it is the easiest way to understand the city on your first night.

metro.title: The metro, six minutes away
metro.text: Tashkent's metro is one of the most beautiful in the world and costs a few thousand som a ride. The nearest station to the Amir Timur Loft is six minutes on foot, eight from the Tashkent City Panorama, which means Chorsu Bazaar, the Kosmonavtlar station mosaics and the whole eastern half of the city are reachable without arranging anything in advance.

chorsu.title: Chorsu Bazaar and the old city
chorsu.text: Four metro stops from the apartments the city changes character completely: the blue dome of Chorsu, mountains of dried apricots, bread stamped in wooden moulds, and behind it the Khast Imam complex with the Uthman Quran. Guests who plan a lazy morning here usually end up staying until the afternoon.

park.title: Tashkent City Park
park.text: The newest part of the centre, built around a lake with fountains that run after dark, glass towers on one side and lawns on the other. From the Tashkent City Panorama it is a fifteen-minute walk and the view of it from the sixteenth floor is the reason most guests book that apartment. The airport is a twenty-five-minute drive from either address.

how-it-works.title: Booking takes about four minutes
how-it-works.lead: There is no form on this page, no account to create and no card to enter. The whole thing happens in one WhatsApp thread with the person who owns the keys.

message.title: Send us your dates
message.text: Tap any booking button and WhatsApp opens with the apartment already named. Tell us the dates, how many of you there are and roughly when you land. We answer with real availability, the total price and the exact address.

confirm.title: We confirm and hold it
confirm.text: Once you say yes the apartment comes off the calendar. No deposit is required, no card is charged, and if your plans change you tell us in the same thread. We will also ask whether you want a driver waiting at the airport.

checkin.title: Let yourself in
checkin.text: On the day of arrival we send the entrance code and a photo of the door. Self check-in works at three in the morning as easily as at three in the afternoon, and one of us is a ten-minute drive away if anything needs sorting.

amir-timur-loft.title: Amir Timur Loft
amir-timur-loft.summary: A two-bedroom apartment on the eighth floor, ten minutes on foot from Amir Timur Square and the Broadway pedestrian street.
amir-timur-loft.photo: Warm daylight interior of a two-bedroom Tashkent apartment: cream plaster walls, a low oak coffee table, a deep terracotta leather armchair, a floor lamp with a white linen shade, sheer curtains diffusing afternoon light, a framed abstract print above a sideboard, ceramic vases. Editorial interiors photography, warm white balance, soft natural light, faint film grain, no people, 16:10 landscape.

paragraphs.intro: This is the apartment most guests book when there are more than two of them. Seventy-four square metres split into two separate bedrooms, a living room that comfortably seats five, and two full bathrooms, so nobody is queueing in the morning before a mountain day.
paragraphs.space: The living room faces a quiet inner courtyard rather than the road, which matters more than it sounds in a city centre. Both bedrooms have blackout curtains, the kitchen is set up for actual cooking rather than reheating, and the desk by the window has a power socket and enough light to work a full day if you need to.
paragraphs.area: Everything you came to Tashkent for is walkable from the front door. Amir Timur Square is ten minutes away, the Broadway pedestrian street runs off it, and the nearest metro station puts Chorsu Bazaar four stops away. When you book a tour with us, the driver collects you here.

tashkent-city-panorama.title: Tashkent City Panorama
tashkent-city-panorama.summary: A one-bedroom apartment on the sixteenth floor with a window wall facing the Tashkent City Park towers.
tashkent-city-panorama.photo: High-floor apartment in Tashkent City: a floor-to-ceiling window with the Tashkent City Park towers visible at golden hour, cream bouclé sofa, round marble side table, muted rose throw blanket, minimal styling, pale oak floor. Warm grading, natural light only, no people, 16:10 landscape.

paragraphs.intro: Fifty-two square metres on the sixteenth floor, built around one long window that looks straight at the Tashkent City Park towers. Couples and solo travellers book this one, and a fair number of them extend by a few nights once they have seen the view at sunset.
paragraphs.space: The bedroom is separate rather than a corner of the living room, which is the difference between a studio and somewhere you can actually live for a week. The building has a lift, a guarded lobby and free parking in the courtyard, and the flat itself is quiet enough on the sixteenth floor that street noise never reaches it.
paragraphs.area: Tashkent City Park is a fifteen-minute walk and is at its best in the evening when the fountains are lit. The metro is close enough that you can be at Chorsu Bazaar in under half an hour without ever booking a taxi, and the airport is a twenty-five-minute drive when it is time to leave.
